intro: This course covered why complaints matter, what the law and regulator expect, and how to receive, report and learn from them well.
points: When a complaint reveals possible abuse or neglect, safeguarding always takes priority and must be reported straight away, never treated as just a complaint.
Report every complaint, even minor or informal ones — it is not your job to filter out what may reveal a pattern.
Stay calm and non-defensive, listen fully, and offer a sincere apology, which is not an admission of legal liability.
Never promise a specific outcome; record the facts accurately without your own judgement and pass them to the right person.
Handling complaints is a legal duty under the 2009 Regulations and CQC Regulation 16, with candour required when things go wrong.
Learn from complaints to improve care, and point anyone still unhappy to the Local Government and Social Care Ombudsman.
